Numeric values of video type constants plus capability flags plus echo flag plus generic write-life constants plus poison delta plus thread info layout are not shown.

findings.text: Three RTC helpers in this configuration are inert success shims. Registering NVMEM for a device and adding one attribute group or several attribute groups each complete immediately with zero status and no observable state change, indicating optional functionality compiled out.

A small netlink send wrapper tolerates an absent buffer. When the supplied socket buffer reference is null the helper reports zero and performs no transmission; otherwise it forwards the buffer together with network namespace plus destination identifier plus multicast group plus echo flag to the underlying send routine and returns that result.

In this build the global RTNL ownership test unconditionally reports held, so derived read-side helpers treat the lock as present. One macro family performs a checked dereference and a second performs a protected dereference and a third replaces a pointer, each parameterized by that ownership predicate. A diagnostic macro warns once with file and line when the per-network assertion fails.

Per-network RTNL control has two shapes. One shape defines checked dereference and replacement helpers that consult a per-network held predicate. The fallback shape provides empty low-level primitives and implements network-scoped lock plus unlock plus trylock plus killable lock by delegating to the corresponding global operations, maps the network assertion to the global assertion, makes workqueue flush a no-op, and aliases network dereference macros to global forms.

Ingress queue access offers protected and lock-free variants. The protected form requires RTNL held semantics to fetch the device ingress queue pointer, while the RCU form fetches the same pointer without that requirement for read-side traversal.
The transmit queue skip query is constant. Regardless of its boolean input it reports false, meaning the caller never takes the skip path in this configuration.
Forwarding database dump iteration carries two positional cursors. The context records an interface index and a table offset, both as unsigned long values, allowing resumption across calls.

Netlink notification need combines echo and listener presence. Listener presence is determined by consulting the per-network RTNL socket for the given group. Need is true when the echo flag is set in the supplied netlink flags or when at least one listener exists.

Runtime verification defines small numeric selectors and limits. Automaton name length is thirty two and racing-event retry limit is three. Monitor scope uses zero for global and then one plus two plus three for per-CPU plus per-task plus per-object respectively.

A deterministic automaton monitor tracks a boolean enabled flag plus a current state number. The flag indicates whether observation is active and the number identifies the present automaton position, advancing under externally defined events.

Linear-time monitor state in the enabled shape holds three fixed bitmaps sized by limits of thirty two atoms and thirty two automaton states. One bitmap records reachable states and two track known versus unknown atomic propositions. Validity holds when any word of the state bitmap is non-zero. Completeness holds when every word of the unknown bitmap is zero. The disabled shape is an empty type with no members.

Hybrid automaton monitor in the enabled shape embeds a deterministic monitor and a single element environment store of sixty four bit values, plus a choice between a high resolution timer and a wheel timer. Timer kind uses zero for none and then one plus two for wheel plus high resolution respectively, with environment length of one. The disabled shape is an empty type.

Per-task monitoring multiplexes the three monitor kinds in a union, holding exactly one of deterministic or linear-time or hybrid state at a time. An initialization helper expands to the configured count of per-task monitors.

A reactor couples a name and descriptive text with a formatted reaction callback and linkage for a global list. A monitor couples identity strings and an enabled flag with enable plus disable plus reset operations, list linkage, a parent pointer for hierarchy, and a debug filesystem root. When reactor support is configured it additionally holds a reactor reference and a formatted reaction entry.
The reaction entry in this configuration discards its arguments. Invoking it with a monitor and message performs no action and returns no value.

Write lifetime hints form a packed enumeration with six ordered levels from unset through none plus short plus medium plus long to extreme, followed by a count sentinel. Each level aliases a corresponding generic lifetime constant.

A real-time reader-writer base combines an atomic reader counter with an underlying real-time mutex. Static initialization seeds the counter to the reader bias and initializes the embedded mutex. Dynamic initialization performs the same two steps procedurally.

Lock state is derived solely from the reader counter. Locked means the counter differs from reader bias. Write locked means it exactly equals writer bias. Contended means it is positive, indicating either bias cleared or waiter presence.
Reader bias sets the top bit of a thirty two bit word while writer bias sets the next bit below it, leaving lower bits for counting and state.

Framebuffer location handling distinguishes capability and size rules. Presence holds only for two video kinds, namely vector linear and EFI. Base address combines a low thirty two bit field with an optional high extension gated by a sixty four bit capability flag. The setter splits a sixty four bit address into low and high halves and maintains that flag accordingly. Size uses the stored value directly except for one vector kind where it shifts left by sixteen.

Video kind classification first filters to a known allowlist of fourteen firmware types and otherwise yields zero. Display detection returns zero when VGA output is off or when text geometry is missing, decodes mode seven as mono variants based on a BIOS register low byte, and otherwise distinguishes sixteen color EGA versus VGA by output flag before falling back to CGA. VBE non-VGA status reflects a single attribute bit. Power-management table base is zero for low segments and otherwise segment shifted plus offset.
Screen information resource limit is three entries.
Platform fixups are inert and PCI lookup reports absence. Applying fixups performs no action and resolving the display PCI device always yields null in this configuration.

Shadow call stack sizing uses order zero so allocation equals one page, with allocation flags combining normal kernel memory and zeroing. End canary is a fixed small constant adjusted by a poison offset. Task accessors obtain base and stack pointer from thread information.

Shadow stack integrity rests on a trailing magic word. Reset restores the stack pointer to the base for task reuse. The magic location is the final word of the allocation. Corruption is reported when bytes used reach allocation size minus one or when the stored magic differs from expected, covering overflow and overwrite.

Dynamic shadow stack support is gated by build configuration and a runtime branch. One build queries a static branch when dynamic support is enabled and otherwise reports fixed values, with the enabled query returning true when dynamic support is absent and otherwise following the dynamic query. Alternate builds constantly report not dynamic or not enabled.

When shadow stacks are unavailable all management operations are inert. Allocation yields null, freeing plus initialization plus release do nothing, preparation reports success, reset does nothing, and corruption checks always report healthy.

Stream control common headers use network byte orders. The fixed header carries source plus destination ports plus verification tag plus checksum with sixteen and thirty two bit widths. The chunk header carries an eight bit type plus eight bit flags plus sixteen bit length in network order. The parameter header carries sixteen bit type and length. A helper derives the transport header pointer from a socket buffer as the fixed header.

Chunk identifiers assign zero through fourteen to data plus initiation plus selective acknowledgement plus heartbeat pair plus abort plus shutdown trio plus error plus cookie pair plus congestion signals, with authentication at fifteen and interleaved data at sixty four and forward acknowledgements plus address plus stream reconfiguration plus padding at high values one ninety two plus one ninety three plus one ninety four plus one twenty eight plus one thirty plus one thirty two respectively.

Unknown chunk handling encodes action in the top two bits with four outcomes from discard through discard with error plus skip to skip with error, masked by the top bits. A single low flag bit marks the T option, tested by examining the chunk flags field.

Parameter identifiers cover heartbeat info plus address types plus cookies plus hostname plus capability discovery plus security plus mobility plus stream reset, with small values one plus five through nine plus eleven plus twelve for legacy items, high-bit values around thirty two thousand for ECN plus random plus chunk list plus HMAC plus extension list, higher values around forty nine thousand for forward support plus address operations plus adaptation indication, and mid values thirteen through eighteen for reset requests plus responses plus stream additions, all stored network ordered. Unknown parameter action similarly uses top two bits with four outcomes and a matching mask.

Data transfer layouts pair a chunk header with a payload header. The classic form holds transmission number plus stream plus sequence numbers plus payload identifier. The interleaved form holds transmission number plus stream plus reserved field plus message identifier and a choice between payload identifier and fragment sequence. Each has a wrapping chunk structure combining headers.
Data fragmentation uses two low bits for middle plus last plus first plus unfragmented states with a mask covering those bits, plus separate bits for unordered delivery and immediate acknowledgement.

Initiation and address parameters share a leading type-length header followed by type-specific bodies. Initiation carries tag plus window plus outbound plus inbound stream counts plus initial sequence, reused by acknowledgement. Address bodies carry IPv4 or IPv6 addresses, cookie preservation carries lifetime increment, hostname carries variable bytes, supported lists carry sixteen bit type arrays or byte chunk arrays, adaptation carries an indication word, HMAC carries identifier array, and cookie plus unrecognized wrappers carry opaque or nested headers.

Acknowledgement and control chunks follow the same header-plus-body pattern. Gap blocks hold start plus end offsets with a union allowing duplicate sequence values. Acknowledgement header holds cumulative sequence plus window plus counts of gaps plus duplicates. Heartbeat wraps an info parameter. Padding and abort carry only a chunk header. Shutdown carries cumulative sequence. Error carries cause plus length with trailing variable data.
